authors: H. R. Fielding, K. A. Fernandes, Amulya V. R., D. Belgayer, A. Misquita, R. Kenny, A. D. Gibson, L. Gamble, B. M. C. Bronsvoort, R. J. Mellanby, I. Handel, D. Rivett, K. Newman, R. King, I. Sayyed, A. Sayed, K. Lad, M. Yaraguda, A. D. Parate, M. K. Balagali, S. Mazeri

mcqs.q: In the first multi-site RCT of free-roaming dog sterilization (58-66% female coverage), what happened to adult dog counts over 2 years?
o: No significant difference vs control sites
mcqs.e: Despite high female coverage, adult FRD counts did not differ from controls, likely confounded by immigration in open populations.

mcqs.q: Which benefits DID the single intensive campaign produce?
o: Fewer puppies, fewer lactating females, less nuisance barking
mcqs.e: The campaign reduced puppies, lactating females, and barking complaints even without lowering adult counts.

mcqs.q: What is the key lesson for one-off sterilization in open populations?
o: A single campaign reliably halves the population
Sustained, repeated effort is needed; one-off campaigns are unlikely to reduce size
mcqs.e: Intense single campaigns require heavy investment but won't shrink open populations alone; ongoing effort is required.

authors: Weerakorn Thichumpa, Anuwat Wiratsudakul, Saranath Lawpoolsri, Yanin Limpanont, Weerapong Thanapongtharm, Lauren M. Smith, Sarawut Maneewong, Wirichada Pan-ngum

mcqs.q: Per the Thailand model, which sterilization strategy most reduced the total dog population?
o: Targeting female dogs across indoor/outdoor/stray classes
mcqs.e: Female-targeted sterilization across all classes cut the total population by >50% over 5 years.

mcqs.q: How did the two female-sterilization strategies compare on cost vs current practice?
o: Cost-saving over time as the population declined
mcqs.e: Total sterilization/vaccination costs fell as the population shrank, making female-focused programs cost-saving.

mcqs.q: What rabies vaccine coverage was modeled alongside sterilization?
mcqs.e: The integrated scenario paired 80% rabies vaccine coverage with sterilization for rabies prevention.

authors: Elly Hiby, Tuntikorn Rungpatana, Alicja Izydorczyk, Valerie Benka, Craig Rooney

mcqs.q: What effect pattern did CNVR intensity show on Bangkok residents' perceptions?
o: Dose-dependent: more rounds, fewer perceived roaming dogs/puppies and lower bite odds
mcqs.e: More CNVR rounds correlated with perceived population declines and lower odds of reporting a dog bite.

mcqs.q: What did the study conclude about owned dogs?
o: Owned dogs are irrelevant to street populations
Owned, free-roaming dogs contribute substantially and must be included in management
mcqs.e: Owned roaming dogs feed the street population, so responsible-ownership measures must be integrated.

mcqs.q: Which management approach did most residents prefer?
mcqs.e: The majority reported sterilisation as their preferred free-roaming dog management approach.

mcqs.q: Why are progestins no longer the preferred feline contraceptive?
o: They risk uterine infection, mammary tumors, and metabolic complications
mcqs.e: Progestins carry significant adverse effects including pyometra, mammary tumors, and metabolic problems.

mcqs.q: Which reversible agent is highlighted as a safer alternative to surgical sterilization?
mcqs.e: GnRH agonists reversibly suppress reproduction and are a safer, more flexible alternative to spay.

mcqs.q: What is the status of feline immunocontraceptive vaccines per the abstract?
mcqs.e: Immunocontraceptive vaccines are an emerging, still-developing technology offering scalable hope.

authors: William A. Stocker, Lauren Olenick, Shreya Maskey, Denise Skrombolas, Haitong Luan, Sophie G. Harrison, Matt Wilson, Anne Traas, Mark Heffernan, Samantha Busfield, Kelly L. Walton, Craig A. Harrison

mcqs.q: In adult queens, what was the effect of the AAV-delivered AMH analog on conception versus pregnancy?
o: Did not block conception but was incompatible with maintaining pregnancy
mcqs.e: Supraphysiologic AMH allowed conception but prevented maintenance of pregnancy, an imperfect contraceptive.

mcqs.q: How long were elevated AMH levels sustained after a single injection?
mcqs.e: A single IM dose raised AMH >1000-fold, sustained for about 9 months.

mcqs.q: What ovarian changes accompanied high AMH?
o: Abnormal estrus, cyst formation, declining antral follicles
mcqs.e: High AMH caused abnormal cyclicity, non-follicular cysts, and progressive antral follicle decline.

authors: Philippe Godin, Nicholas Nagykery, Natalie Sicher, Julie L. Barnes, Amy G. Miller, Christina Bunner, Amy K. Thompson, Motohiro Kano, Guangping Gao, Dan Wang, Patricia K. Donahoe, Linda Rhodes, David A. Brake, Thomas J. Conlon, William F. Swanson, Lindsey M. Vansandt, David Pepin

mcqs.q: In PREPUBERTAL kittens, what did a single AAV-AMH injection achieve in adulthood?
mcqs.e: A single prepubertal dose fully prevented pregnancy once females reached adulthood (up to 21 months).

mcqs.q: By what mechanism was sterility induced in mated females?
o: Preventing breeding-induced ovulation and the luteal progesterone rise
mcqs.e: Sustained AMH blocked breeding-induced ovulation and luteal-phase progesterone, causing sterility.

mcqs.q: What was the effect on male spermatogenesis and physical growth?
mcqs.e: The injection was well tolerated, sparing male spermatogenesis and not impacting growth.

authors: Marco Tabbi, Alessandro Troisi, Domenico Fugazzotto, Romina Marcoccia, Giorgia Pettina, Simone Minniti, Girolamo Messina, Temy Coppola, Gaetano Principato, Federica Arrigo, Giuseppe Barillaro, Daniele Troiano, Angela Polisca, Viola Zappone

mcqs.q: How did early gonadectomy (<12 months) affect intervertebral disc herniation risk in French Bulldogs?
mcqs.e: Early-gonadectomized dogs had significantly higher IVDH risk than intact dogs.

mcqs.q: Which group showed the strongest association with IVDH?
mcqs.e: Early-gonadectomized females had the largest odds ratio (9.84) versus intact females.

mcqs.q: What clinical implication does the study suggest?
o: Carefully consider/delay gonadectomy timing in predisposed chondrodystrophic breeds
mcqs.e: Age at gonadectomy should be weighed carefully in chondrodystrophic breeds prone to IVDH.

mcqs.q: Cranial cruciate ligament disease risk was greatest in dogs with which hormone exposure?
mcqs.e: Risk was highest with the least cumulative hormone exposure, i.e., earliest gonadectomy.

mcqs.q: How was the relationship between hormone exposure and CrCLD risk best described?
mcqs.e: A generalised additive model showed a nonlinear association in both sexes.

mcqs.q: At roughly what age did CrCLD risk reach its minimum?
mcqs.e: Risk minima fell near 1054 days (females) and 805 days (males), about 2.9 and 2.2 years.

authors: Valerie A. Benka, John M. Sahrmann, Katherine Rieke, Joyce R. Briggs, Nathaniel Spofford, Stephen Zawistowski, Audrey Ruple, Stefano Romagnoli, Jo Ann Morrison
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association

mcqs.q: In toy/small breeds, how did neutering at 3 or 6 months compare with neutering at 1 year or older for overweight/obese risk?
o: Lower than or not significantly different from later neuter
mcqs.e: Early neuter in small breeds carried hazard ratios no worse than later neuter, supporting pediatric neuter safety.

mcqs.q: What did the study find about underlying obesity susceptibility?
o: Substantial breed variation (Pugs, Goldens, Labs highest)
mcqs.e: Underlying overweight/obese susceptibility varied by breed, highest in Pugs, Goldens, and Labs.

mcqs.q: What was the overall conclusion about gonadectomy?
o: It offers significant individual and population benefits, with breed-tailored weight counseling
mcqs.e: Gonadectomy provides meaningful benefits despite non-uniform, breed-dependent obesity risk.

authors: Rui Jardim, Bruno Colaco, Maria de Lurdes Pinto, Sofia Alves-Pimenta

mcqs.q: What was the single strongest predictor of adoption in this Portuguese shelter?
o: Length of stay (longer reduced adoption odds)
mcqs.e: Extended length of stay markedly reduced adoption odds and drove overcrowding.

mcqs.q: How much more likely were microchipped animals to be returned to owners?
mcqs.e: Microchipped animals were 71 times more likely to be reunited with owners.

mcqs.q: Which data-driven strategies did the authors recommend?
o: Reduce length of stay and enforce microchipping
mcqs.e: Cutting LOS and enforcing microchipping were key levers to improve flow-through and welfare.

mcqs.q: Why are conventional shelter LOS calculations biased for fixed calendar periods?
o: They count only animals whose stay ended in the window, ignoring those still in care
mcqs.e: Counting only completed stays misrepresents LOS by excluding animals present but not yet discharged.

mcqs.q: Which statistical approach is proposed to compute LOS correctly?
mcqs.e: Survival methods with left-truncation and right-censoring include all animals present for any part of the period.

mcqs.q: What did the corrected method reveal about post-COVID dog LOS in Orange County?
o: A real LOS increase not explained by intake demographics
mcqs.e: A genuine post-COVID LOS rise appeared, plausibly tied to restricted visitor access rather than intake changes.

authors: K. Pasteur, N. O. Widmar, C. V. Tran, C. C. Croney

mcqs.q: How did most survey respondents define 'access to care'?
o: Provider availability, ease of communication, and affordability
mcqs.e: Access was defined chiefly by availability (78%), communication (78%), and affordability (75%), not cost alone.

mcqs.q: What did over half of care-seekers report about their veterinarian?
mcqs.e: 54.7% of care-seekers reported distrusting their veterinarian despite often being satisfied with pet care.

mcqs.q: Which care-delivery model do the findings support?
mcqs.e: Most owners would accept techs or mid-tier professionals rather than forgo care, supporting expanded-role models.
